tiles: Scale, quiet wonder, and the face as terrain
Six pieces I kept for their strangeness
challenge: Surrealism has always interested me because the best of it isn't weird for its own sake — it uses strangeness to say something about being a person. I wanted to spend some time with that idea and see if I could get closer to understanding it.
approach: I read into the movement and the artists who built it, then drafted many variations around the idea of a head that's also a place — a landscape, a world with weather. I kept the ones that felt quiet and curious rather than loud, and that I personally found moving.
result: Six pieces came out of it that I genuinely love — calm, strange, a little dreamy. They're available as prints in case anyone else finds the same quiet wonder in them that I did.
